what: decomp-permuter re-run on the p6 five-arm switch (0x8004fd1c), scored with the word metric

settings.file: f.toml (NOT READ -- get_settings() opens settings.toml only; [base] weights applied)

metric.pipeline: cc1 -O2 -G 0 -mips2 -mcpu=r4300 -> as -g -> ld, then word-compare against the image

run_image_objective.objective: target.o built by make_target.py from the image's own 98 words (392 B, byte-identical, no relocs)

verdict: With the PROXY objective the permuter never passes 94/98 in 226 000 iterations; with the IMAGE objective it reaches 98/98 (byte-exact) in 83 834. The plateau was the objective, not the tool. M300's 'cannot reach this shape by randomisation' is retracted -- and the winner is a DIFFERENT shape from the hand reconstruction: it keeps a `new_var` temporary in case 4 instead of transposing two statements.
correction: M303: every run recorded here used the default `[base]` weights, not `gcc` -- the settings file was named `f.toml` and `get_settings()` reads `settings.toml`. The proxy-vs-image comparison is unaffected; the 'under both weightings' phrasing in M300 is withdrawn.
